subject: Meditech: Exhibit for operational handover and alternative to escrow
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@meditech.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@meditech.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Meditech MSA redlines + operational handover ask

Hi Jordan / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal reviewed the MSA and has a few asks related to private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Attached are our redlines (Meditech_MSA_Redlines.pdf). Key items:

- Our procurement team needs either an escrow-style proof of operational handover or an auditable snapshot transfer process for disaster recovery.
- We require a narrow audit window and an attestation that no vendor operators can access customer data post-handover without documented escalation.
- Exhibit describing steps for rolling back to a known-good snapshot during a breach.

Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide and a rough timeline to deliver a proposed Exhibit for the Order Form? We have a procurement deadline of May 20.

Rajiv
Meditech Health

Attachment: Meditech_MSA_Redlines.pdf

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@meditech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-01T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Meditech MSA redlines + operational handover ask

Rajiv — thanks for the redlines and the timeline. Laura / Priyom — looping you both in to coordinate responses and a proposed Exhibit.

High-level proposal from our side (to discuss):
- We can provide a documented Operational Handover Exhibit (new Exhibit B) covering: snapshot transfer process, key custody options, audit window, operator access controls, and rollback playbook.
- As an alternative to full-code escrow, we can offer a cryptographically signed snapshot + manifest delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket (KMS-wrapped) and an attestation from Redwood engineering describing how to reproduce the image. This reduces friction for customers who prefer faster handover without third-party escrow.

Deliverables I suggest this week: draft Exhibit B (legal), engineering runbook excerpt (Priyom), and an evidence checklist for procurement (to send to Anne / Meditech counsel). If Meditech insists on third-party escrow, we can surface options but need legal to evaluate redline changes.

Can we aim for a draft by EOD May 4? Also adding HubSpot deal HSP-5821 here for visibility: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/5821

—Jordan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed timeline (inline)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@meditech.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-02T10:45:00Z
Subject: Draft Exhibit B: Operational Handover (v1)

Jordan / Rajiv / Team — attaching a first pass: ExhibitB-OperationalHandover-v1.docx. High level comments for discussion: 

1) License scope: we need to keep model license and runtime IP protections. Exhibit should not expand to provide source code or proprietary model training artifacts.
2) Access boundary: define "operator access" narrowly and tie to documented emergency escalation process. Any remote debugging or console access should require dual-auth and a documented audit trace.
3) Evidence types: prefer a signed manifest + KMS-wrapped snapshot transfer as an "escrow-lite" option; add a short paragraph that permits third-party escrow if customer insists but requires a separate SOW and cost schedule.
4) Audit window: propose 48 hours for snapshot retrieval requests, with an optional on-site audit window to be scheduled and costed separately.

I've marked redlines in the attached document. Please review the runbook language (Priyom) and the technical constraints before we send to Meditech counsel. If everyone agrees, I will produce a tracked redline doc for the MSA and Order Form (will use redlines-tracked.docx).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: ExhibitB-OperationalHandover-v1.docx

From: Anne Sullivan <anne.sullivan@ogclaw.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@meditech.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@meditech.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T15:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Draft Exhibit B: Operational Handover (v1)

Laura / Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few notes from Meditech counsel:

- Evidence checklist: we need a concrete list of artifacts. Examples we expect: checksums of images, chain-of-custody manifest, operator access logs for the preceding 90 days, signed attestation from an authorized Redwood engineer. Please add these to Exhibit B or an attachment.
- Escrow vs attestation: Meditech will accept an "attestation + signed manifest" only if a third-party custodian can verify retrieval and we can run a retrieval test within the contract term. Is Redwood willing to agree to an annual retrieval test (or an agreed cadence)?
- Audit rights: request language for a remote forensic audit (read-only) plus an option for a single on-site verification during a paid audit window.

I'll attach our evidence checklist template — please fill and return (evidence-checklist.csv). Also need confirmation on whether Redwood will require a separate SOW for any third-party escrow fees.

Anne Sullivan
Outside Counsel for Meditech
OGC Law

Attachment: evidence-checklist.csv

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, Anne Sullivan <anne.sullivan@ogclaw.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@meditech.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T11:35:00Z
Subject: RE: Draft Exhibit B: Operational Handover (v1) — engineering details

Anne / Laura / Jordan — technical clarifications from Eng: 

- Snapshot transfer: we can generate a read-only snapshot of the runtime environment (container images + KV snapshot) and publish a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums). The artifact will be uploaded to a customer-provided S3 bucket, encrypted with the customer's KMS key. Transfer will include a signed envelope from Redwood (HMAC + cert).
- Retrieval test: we can support an annual retrieval test executed by Redwood engineering and observed by customer or their third-party custodian. Test process will be captured in the runbook excerpt attached.
- Operator access: Redwood will create ephemeral operator keys scoped to the incident with full audit logging turned on. Keys expire and require manager approval + two-factor sign-off for session initiation.
- Timeline: we can produce the runbook and tech annex by EOD May 5. Production of the signed artifacts and a dry-run can be scheduled the week of May 18 (subject to procurement sign-off).

See attached runbook-snippet.txt for the small sample of the retrieval steps and key rotation notes.

Priyom Das
Senior SWE, Deployment — Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-snippet.txt

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@meditech.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@meditech.com>, Anne Sullivan <anne.sullivan@ogclaw.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-06T16:45:00Z
Subject: Next steps and asks: Exhibit B finalization + pricing concession

Team — thanks for the thorough feedback. Proposed next steps: 

1) Laura to finalize tracked redlines for the MSA and Order Form (I will send to Rajiv & Anne). Expecting redlines-tracked.docx back by May 7 COB.
2) Priyom / Eng to deliver the full runbook + tech annex (May 5 deliverable provided; full doc by May 11).
3) Redwood to commit to an annual retrieval test and a documented remote audit window (48 hours) as part of Exhibit B; third-party escrow remains an option with a separate SOW and fee schedule.

Commercial ask: because the attestation + signed-manifest approach reduces our operational burden vs full escrow, Sales recommends a modest one-time credit if Meditech accepts the attestation path in lieu of third-party escrow. Rishi — can you advise on credit approvals or whether this needs leadership sign-off?

Rajiv / Anne — once we have Laura's tracked redlines, can we target an executed Order Form by May 20 to keep to procurement timelines? I will attach the tracked redlines in my next email (redlines-tracked.docx) and post the DocuSign link once legal signs off.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines-tracked.docx
